descripcion_geo: The largest river in Western Asia, it originates in Anatolia and empties into the Persian Gulf after 2,700 km. Eastern border of the promised land.
importancia_estrategica: Northeastern border of the promised land and axis of the great Mesopotamian empires.

historias.titulo: The Euphrates as the border of promise
historias.descripcion: God promises Abraham that his descendants will inherit the land 'from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.'

historias.titulo: Exile by the Rivers by Babylon
historias.descripcion: The deportees of Judah sit by the rivers of Babylon (the Euphrates and its canals) and weep for Zion.
The Apocalypse uses the Euphrates as an eschatological border: its waters dry up to make way for the kings of the east.

personajes.descripcion: God promised Abraham the land up to the Euphrates as an inheritance for his descendants.
He turned the Euphrates into the heart of the largest Empire in the ancient world.
He crossed the Euphrates to conquer Babylon; He freed the Jews from exile.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Sacred River of Mesopotamia; limit of divine promise and eschatological symbol in the Apocalypse.

judaismo.descripcion: The Euphrates is one of the four rivers that watered the Garden of Eden (Gen 2:14).
judaismo.significado_teologico: The Euphrates is one of the four rivers that watered the Garden of Eden (Gen 2:14).

cristianismo.descripcion: The Apocalypse uses it as a border that dries up at the time of the end (Rev 16:12).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The Apocalypse uses it as a border that dries up at the time of the end (Rev 16:12).

islam.descripcion: Islam places the Euphrates in the land of the prophets; Traditions say that it will hide treasures at the end of time.
islam.significado_teologico: Islam places the Euphrates in the land of the prophets; Traditions say that it will hide treasures at the end of time.
